tweet.text:
$INIO 

I POUNDED THE TABLE ON $FPS FOR MONTHS.

I’ve got more up my sleeve just subscribe. Not many are as early as me.

Posting more to subscribers today or miss out tomorrow. It’s 1$

Will you listen this time? 

I seen @CKCapitalxx make a post and credit to them for seeing potential he’s almost at 100k because he finds opportunities like these.

But for the record I’m going on two months of telling you all and the subscribers to buy. 

We’re early. Follow @NURadu_ too just not many eyes! 

INNIO is exactly the kind of overlooked AI infrastructure opportunity I want people paying attention to. 

The market is focused on chips and data centers, but what happens when those data centers cannot get enough power online? 

INNIO supplies the engines that help solve that bottleneck. At roughly $19–$20, the stock sits well below its $27 IPO price despite a rapidly expanding backlog.

The numbers are getting difficult to ignore. Equipment backlog reached approximately $6.6B in June 2026, up from roughly $1B at the end of 2024. 

Commitments and reservations reportedly exceed 15 GW, with approximately $1.4B in customer prepayments and first-half equipment book-to-bill around 4.4x. INNIO is targeting $3.8B–$3.9B in 2026 revenue and $720M–$740M in adjusted EBITDA.

The J624 is a key piece of the story, delivering roughly 4.5–5 MW per modular natural-gas engine with rapid load response. Data centers cannot always wait years for grid connections, and INNIO shipped approximately 3.4 GW last year while expanding toward 10 GW of annual capacity by 2030. Its Wisconsin expansion includes more than $300M in announced investment.

Now look at the earnings power. Services represented approximately 48% of 2025 revenue and around 65% of segment profit, creating a potentially powerful recurring-revenue stream as the installed base grows. 

Management is targeting equipment-margin recovery into the high teens by year-end 2026, while full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance implies roughly a 19% margin at the midpoint.

The latest Aggreko extension adds more visibility, with at least 450 MW of Jenbacher Type 4 capacity agreed for 2027, J620 engines beginning in 2028, and a multiyear service agreement through a partnership extended to 2031. 

The entire 450 MW commitment has not been identified as data-center-specific demand, but it reinforces the broader equipment and aftermarket opportunity. INNIO’s roughly $14B–$15B market cap also stands out against Bloom Energy’s much larger valuation despite broadly comparable 2026 revenue expectations.

Why is the market skeptical? 

Sponsor ownership remains above 80%, the limited public float faces a potential late-November lockup overhang, and customer concentration, tariffs, permitting, and execution remain real risks. 

But does that justify discounting a business with a $6.6B equipment backlog and a multiyear capacity expansion?

I pounded the table on $FPS for months. I’m watching the next opportunity in the same spirit: overlooked infrastructure, a critical niche, expanding demand, and a market that may not fully appreciate the numbers yet.

Will you listen this time? 😤

Rip salad soon. Double bottom.
